recommended_treatments: Rest in a quiet, dark room to reduce sensory stimulation.
Apply a cool cloth or ice pack to the forehead or temples.
Stay hydrated (aim for 2.0L - 2.5L of water daily).
Perform gentle neck range-of-motion stretching exercises.
Incorporate deep breathing techniques and progressive muscle relaxation.
avoid: Excessive screen time (mobile, laptop, TV) during pain flares.
Caffeine overuse or sudden caffeine withdrawal.
red_flags: Headaches accompanied by high fever, stiff neck, confusion, or seizures.
Difficulty speaking, numbness, or weakness on one side of the face/body.

recommended_treatments: Apply a warm compress or heating pad for 15-20 minutes to relax stiff muscles.
Perform slow, gentle head tilts and side-to-side turns.
Optimize workstation ergonomics (screen at eye level, sit back in chair).
Use a supportive, contouring neck pillow during sleep.
avoid: Cradling a phone between your shoulder and ear.
High-impact or jarring activities that strain the neck vertebrae.
red_flags: Pain radiating down both arms accompanied by weakness or numbness.
New clumsiness in hands or difficulty walking/maintaining balance.

recommended_treatments: Use ice therapy for acute flare-ups to reduce active joint inflammation.
Do gentle pendulum exercises (swinging the arm gently back and forth).
Maintain a upright posture; pull shoulders back and down throughout the day.
avoid: Sleeping on the painful side shoulder.
Heavy overhead lifting or repetitive reaching.
red_flags: Shoulder pain accompanied by tightness, pressure, or squeezing in the chest.
Inability to move or lift the arm at all.

recommended_treatments: Engage in structured low-impact physical exercise (aerobic walking, yoga, stretching) as recommended by the 2023 WHO low back pain guidelines.
Apply dry heat (heating pad) to soothe muscle spasms and stiffness.
Incorporate mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) or cognitive behavioral strategies to help manage pain perception.
Ensure proper lifting technique (bend at the knees, not at the waist).
avoid: Prolonged bed rest beyond 48 hours, as active movement improves long-term recovery.
Slouching or sitting in soft, unsupportive sofas for long durations.
red_flags: Loss of bowel or bladder control (incontinence) or sudden numbness in the groin/saddle area.
Back pain accompanied by unexplained weight loss or high fever.
Severe pain that does not change with position or rest.

recommended_treatments: Perform low-impact exercises like swimming, stationary cycling, or water aerobics.
Apply cold packs to reduce joint swelling after activity.
Maintain a healthy weight to reduce the mechanical load placed on joint cartilage.
Wear supportive footwear with cushioned soles.
avoid: Deep squatting or kneeling on hard surfaces.
red_flags: Inability to bear weight on the knee or feeling that the joint is 'giving out'.
Severe swelling, redness, and heat around the knee joint accompanied by a fever.
